subject: medicine
title: Acute nephritic syndrome, post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, and IgA nephropathy

steps.tx: Acute inflammatory injury within the glomerular capillary tuft produces a classic constellation of physical and urinary manifestations. Characterized as **Nephritic syndrome**, the clinical presentation features macroscopic or microscopic haematuria displaying dysmorphic red blood cells and diagnostic red cell casts on urine sediment examination. Accompanying inflammatory capillary occlusion impairs filtration clearance, precipitating secondary renal sodium and water retention that causes arterial hypertension, periorbital facial puffiness, oliguria, and subnephrotic proteinuria (typically under three point five grams per twenty-four hours).
steps.say: Acute inflammatory injury within glomerular capillaries causes a classic constellation of physical and urinary signs. Characterized as Nephritic syndrome, the clinical presentation features haematuria with dysmorphic red cells and red cell casts. Inflammatory capillary occlusion impairs filtration, driving fluid retention that causes hypertension, periorbital oedema, and subnephrotic proteinuria.

steps.tx: Immune complex deposition following remote pharyngeal or cutaneous bacterial infection triggers diffuse proliferative glomerular endocapillary inflammation. Developing **post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis** (PSGN) follows infection by nephritogenic strains of group A beta-haemolytic streptococci carrying virulence factors like streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxin B. Clinical illness manifests after a characteristic latent period of one to three weeks following pharyngitis, or three to six weeks following cutaneous impetigo. The classically presenting child exhibits smoky or cola-coloured dark urine, periorbital oedema, and elevated blood pressure.
steps.say: Immune complex deposition after remote streptococcal infection causes diffuse glomerular inflammation. Developing post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis follows exposure to nephritogenic strains of group A streptococci. Symptoms appear after a latent period of two weeks following pharyngitis, or four weeks after impetigo, presenting with cola-coloured urine, facial puffiness, and hypertension.

vis.caption: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis presenting with smoky urine and endocapillary proliferation. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Serological assessment confirms prior streptococcal exposure and validates alternate pathway complement consumption in suspected post-streptococcal disease. Evaluating **PSGN serological markers** reveals elevated anti-streptolysin O (ASO) titres in over eighty percent of post-pharyngitis presentations, while anti-DNase B titres provide superior sensitivity following cutaneous impetigo infections. Concurrently, transient hypocomplementaemia marked by profoundly depressed serum C3 with normal or mildly reduced C4 confirms activation of the alternative complement pathway. Spontaneous normalization of serum C3 levels within six to eight weeks represents a mandatory diagnostic hallmark.
steps.say: Serological evaluation confirms prior streptococcal infection and demonstrates complement activation in post-streptococcal disease. Evaluating PSGN serological markers reveals high anti-streptolysin O titres after pharyngitis, while anti-DNase B titres identify preceding impetigo. Profoundly low serum C3 with normal C4 confirms alternative complement activation, which normalizes within two months.

rows: Superior sensitivity for preceding skin impetigo
Alternative pathway consumption; normalizes in 6-8 weeks
Differentiates PSGN from classic pathway lupus nephritis

steps.tx: Pathological evaluation under light, immunofluorescence, and electron microscopy identifies pathognomonic architectural alterations in post-streptococcal disease. Analyzing **PSGN histopathology** on light microscopy demonstrates diffuse, global hypercellularity caused by endocapillary proliferation of endothelial and mesangial cells combined with neutrophilic infiltration. Immunofluorescence reveals granular, starry-sky or garland-like deposits of immunoglobulin G and C3 along capillary walls and mesangium. Electron microscopy establishes definitive diagnostic confirmation by demonstrating large, discrete subepithelial electron-dense deposits classically described as subepithelial humps.
steps.say: Pathological evaluation across light, fluorescence, and electron microscopy demonstrates classic structural hallmarks in post-streptococcal disease. Analyzing PSGN histopathology on light microscopy shows diffuse hypercellularity from endothelial proliferation and neutrophils. Fluorescence demonstrates starry-sky granular deposits, while electron microscopy confirms diagnostic subepithelial humps.

steps.tx: Abnormal glycosylation of mucosal antibodies triggers the most prevalent primary glomerular disease encountered in global clinical nephrology practice. Known also as **Berger disease**, the condition of **IgA nephropathy** stems from deficient galactosylation of O-linked glycans in the hinge region of circulating immunoglobulin A1. Polymeric galactose-deficient IgA1 molecules act as autoantigens, forming circulating immune complexes with anti-glycan IgG antibodies that deposit within the renal mesangium. Patients characteristically present with episodic macroscopic haematuria coinciding concurrently within twenty-four to forty-eight hours of an upper respiratory tract infection.
steps.say: Abnormal glycosylation of mucosal antibodies causes the most common primary glomerular disease worldwide. Known also as Berger disease, IgA nephropathy results from galactose-deficient IgA1 molecules that form circulating immune complexes. These complexes deposit within the renal mesangium, presenting with episodic gross haematuria coinciding within two days of an upper respiratory infection.

left.title: IgA Nephropathy (Berger Disease)
points: Normal serum complement C3 and C4 levels
Mesangial proliferation with dominant IgA staining

steps.tx: Accurate differential diagnosis between post-infectious and mucosal nephritides relies on the precise temporal relationship between initial mucosal symptoms and urinary discoloration. Comparing **synpharyngitic versus post-infectious** presentations reveals that IgA nephropathy produces synpharyngitic gross haematuria developing simultaneously within one to two days of pharyngeal infection, accompanied by completely normal serum complement concentrations. In sharp contrast, post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis exhibits a mandatory latent interval of one to three weeks following pharyngitis, accompanied by profound depression of circulating serum C3 complement.
steps.say: Accurate differential diagnosis between post-infectious and mucosal nephritides relies on the precise timeline between infection and dark urine. Comparing synpharyngitic versus post-infectious presentations shows that IgA nephropathy produces dark urine within one to two days of throat symptoms, with normal complement levels. In contrast, post-streptococcal disease requires a two-week latency accompanied by low serum C3.

rows: Non-specific viral URI or strenuous exercise

steps.tx: Severe necrotizing glomerular inflammation that drives precipitous deterioration of renal function over a span of days to weeks defines a medical emergency. Characterized as **rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis** (RPGN), this syndromic presentation features acute nephritic sediment, oliguria, and a greater than fifty percent decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate within three months. Pathological examination confirms extensive parietal epithelial crescent formation in greater than fifty percent of glomeruli, compressing capillary tufts and mandating urgent renal biopsy and aggressive immunosuppressive intervention.
steps.say: Severe necrotizing glomerular inflammation driving rapid decline in renal function over weeks constitutes an emergency. Characterized as rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, this syndrome presents with acute nephritic urine, oliguria, and progressive filtration loss. Biopsy demonstrates extensive epithelial crescent formation compressing capillary tufts, requiring urgent immunosuppression.

nodes.label: Acute Nephritic Presentation + Rapid Doubling of Creatinine
Pulse IV Methylprednisolone + Cyclophosphamide / Plasma Exchange

steps.tx: Supportive management of acute post-streptococcal disease focuses on strict fluid control, whereas chronic progressive nephritides require targeted long-term nephroprotection. Implementing **nephritic clinical monitoring** emphasizes sodium restriction and loop diuretics to treat hypertensive volume overload in self-limiting post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis. In chronic IgA nephropathy, sustained proteinuria exceeding zero point seven five to one gram daily warrants maximum-tolerated ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy, SGLT2 inhibitors, and targeted-release oral budesonide to halt progressive glomerular sclerosis.
steps.say: Supportive management of acute post-streptococcal disease focuses on fluid balance, whereas chronic nephritides require long-term nephroprotection. Implementing nephritic clinical monitoring emphasizes dietary sodium restriction and loop diuretics to manage hypertension and fluid retention. In chronic IgA nephropathy, persistent proteinuria requires ACE inhibitors and SGLT2 inhibitors to preserve kidney function.
